target.approvedName: ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit H
functionDescriptions: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons (PubMed:33065002). V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments and in some cell types, is targeted to the plasma membrane, where it promotes acidification of the extracellular environment (By similarity). The V- ATPase complex also acts as an activator for mTORC1 on lysosomal membrane by promoting the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) of the Ragulator complex, thereby enabling mTORC1 recruitment (PubMed:22053050). Subunit H is essential for V-ATPase activity, but not for the assembly of the complex (By similarity). Involved in the endocytosis mediated by clathrin-coated pits, required for the formation of endosomes (PubMed:12032142). {ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:O46563, ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:P41807, ECO:0000269|PubMed:12032142, ECO:0000269|PubMed:22053050, ECO:0000269|PubMed:33065002}.
